title: Anti-Social Behaviour Policy and Procedure
summary: How Silvering prevents and tackles anti-social behaviour, including mandatory risk assessment within 1 working day, response times by category, case reviews, enforcement tools and case closure.
author: P026

version_history.change: Full review; Neighbourhood Standard alignment; victim-centred approach
After RSH inspection: risk assessment mandatory on every case within 1 working day; fortnightly reviews for high-risk cases

blocks.p: Everyone has the right to feel safe in their home and neighbourhood. This policy explains how we prevent and respond to anti-social behaviour (ASB) affecting our residents, in line with the Regulator of Social Housing's Neighbourhood and Community Standard and the Anti-social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014. It applies to all tenures and to behaviour by residents, members of their household and visitors.

ASB is conduct that has caused, or is likely to cause, harassment, alarm or distress to any person, or that causes housing-related nuisance or annoyance. Examples: harassment and threats, hate incidents, drug dealing, criminal damage, persistent noise, and misuse of communal areas. Everyday living noise, children playing and one-off disagreements between neighbours are not usually ASB; we will offer advice and, where helpful, mediation.

rows: Hate incident, domestic abuse, threats of violence, harassment
Within 1 working day of the report
Within 1 working day of the report
Every 10 working days if high risk, otherwise 20
Within 1 working day of the report
table.caption: Table 1: Response standards

blocks.callout: Every ASB case must have a completed risk assessment matrix in Keystone within 1 working day of the first report, whatever the category. A case cannot be progressed past 'Initial contact' without one. High-risk cases must be discussed with the ASB & Tenancy Enforcement Officer the same day.
blocks.title: Mandatory risk assessment

blocks.p: The risk assessment matrix scores the reporter's vulnerability (health, age, disability, previous victimisation, isolation) and the seriousness of the behaviour. A score of 15 or more is high risk. High-risk victims are offered a support plan, referral to Victim Support or a domestic abuse service, and consideration of target hardening (locks, door chains, CCTV doorbells). The assessment is repeated at each case review.

We agree an action plan with the reporter, setting out what we will do, what we ask them to do (such as diary sheets or the noise app) and when we will next contact them. We keep the reporter informed at least at every case review.

bullets: Advice, diary sheets and the noise monitoring app
Mediation through our independent mediation partner
Warning letters and interviews with the alleged perpetrator
Acceptable behaviour agreements (ABAs)
Joint visits and information sharing with the police and the borough council's community safety team
Civil injunctions under Part 1 of the 2014 Act, with power of arrest where there is violence or threat of violence
Partner-led closure orders for premises used for drug dealing or serious nuisance
Possession proceedings, including the absolute ground for ASB (Ground 7A), as a last resort

blocks.p: We close a case when the behaviour has stopped, when we have taken all reasonable action, or when the reporter no longer wishes to proceed. We will discuss closure with the reporter first and write to confirm it. We ask every reporter whether they were satisfied with how the case was handled.
If a resident has reported three or more incidents in six months and feels no action has been taken, they can ask the borough council for an ASB Case Review. We take part fully in these reviews.

All ASB records are held in Keystone Housing and labelled Confidential. Case chronologies used as court evidence must be accurate, dated and factual, with sources. Information is shared with partners under our information sharing agreement and UK GDPR. Do not paste ASB case details into AI tools unless the tool is approved and the file carries the correct sensitivity label.

title: Rent Arrears and Income Recovery Policy
summary: How Silvering supports residents to pay their rent and recovers arrears: early contact, Universal Credit and APA rules, payment arrangements, hardship fund, the pre-action protocol and possession as a last resort.
author: P015

blocks.p: Rent pays for repairs, services and new homes. We want to help residents pay on time and avoid debt. Our approach is **firm but fair**: we contact residents early, help them maximise their income, agree affordable arrangements, and only use legal action as a last resort. Rents rose by {{fact:rent_increase_2627}} in April 2026.

rows: Text or call; check for change of circumstances or UC claim
Friendly letter with offer of help and money advice
Phone call and home visit by the income officer
Affordable arrangement based on an income and expenditure check
Referral to money advice and the hardship fund (up to £500)
8 weeks' arrears with no arrangement, after the pre-action protocol
Notice of Seeking Possession - Income Manager approval required
Monitor the order; support to keep to its terms
table.caption: Table 1: Recovery stages

bullets: When we learn a resident has claimed UC we verify their housing costs on the DWP landlord portal within 2 working days.

We **must** request an Alternative Payment Arrangement (managed payment to landlord) when arrears reach the equivalent of 8 weeks' (2 months') rent, or 1 month's rent where the resident is vulnerable or has repeatedly missed payments.
Where arrears continue we may request third-party deductions for arrears.
We do not take enforcement action while a UC claim is being assessed if the resident is engaging.

blocks.p: Before we start possession proceedings for rent arrears we follow the Pre-Action Protocol for Possession Claims by Social Landlords. We must: contact the resident to discuss the arrears and their circumstances; give clear statements of account; offer help with benefits and money advice; try to agree an affordable arrangement; and consider whether the resident has a disability or other vulnerability. We postpone court action if the resident has a reasonable expectation of benefit that will cover the arrears.

Before any NOSP or court action the income officer must check Keystone for vulnerability flags, open complaints and open safeguarding concerns. Where a resident has an open complaint linked to the arrears (for example about service charges or a disrepair claim) escalation must be paused until the Income Manager has reviewed the case.
Letters must be plain English, non-threatening and include the money advice options. Never use red ink, capitals or the word 'final' on a first letter.

title: Lettings Policy
summary: How Silvering lets its homes through the borough councils' choice-based lettings schemes, nominations, direct lets, affordability checks, refusals, starter tenancies and the Orchard Fields local lettings plan.
author: P028

blocks.p: We aim to let homes quickly, fairly and in a way that creates sustainable tenancies and balanced communities. Empty homes cost us rent and leave families waiting: over the last 12 months the average relet time was {{fact:void_days_avg_12m}} days.

Most of our general needs homes are let through the borough councils' choice-based lettings schemes. Applicants join the council's housing register, are placed in a band, and bid for homes we advertise. Under our nominations agreements the council nominates to 100% of first lets of new-build homes and 75% of relets; the remaining 25% are used for our own transfers and management moves.

bullets: Management transfers: urgent moves for residents at risk of violence, serious harassment or with urgent medical need, approved by the Head of Neighbourhoods.
Decants: temporary or permanent moves because of major works or serious damp and mould.
SilverLiving homes for applicants aged 55+, let through our own waiting list with a support assessment.
Adapted homes, matched to applicants with the right needs through the council's occupational therapy service.

blocks.p: Shortlisted applicants are verified (identity, right to rent, household and income), and an affordability check is completed. Applicants can view before accepting. An applicant who refuses two reasonable offers may be suspended from bidding by the council.

New tenants (other than transfers) receive a 12-month starter tenancy. We carry out a new tenancy visit within 6 weeks and reviews at 4 and 9 months. A starter tenancy may be extended by 6 months if there are concerns.

For the first lets at Orchard Fields phase 1, agreed with the borough council, up to 30% of rented homes may go to working households and no more than 50% of family homes to households with three or more children, to support a balanced new community. {{fact:newbuild_awaiting_let}} homes are still awaiting their first let, mainly because of outstanding defects.

title: Tenancy Sustainment and Vulnerability Policy
summary: How Silvering identifies and records vulnerability, makes reasonable adjustments, supports residents to sustain their tenancies and protects special category data, including in Copilot and other AI tools.
author: P011

blocks.p: Some residents need extra help to keep their home. This policy explains how we identify vulnerability, record it safely, adapt our services and work with partners so that tenancies are sustained and evictions are avoided wherever possible.

Vulnerability can be permanent or temporary. We record it in Keystone using the categories below, with the resident's consent wherever possible: respiratory condition, frailty, hearing or sight, learning disability, mobility, mental health, and domestic abuse survivor. Every member of staff and every operative is expected to notice and report signs of vulnerability, such as a home in poor condition, confusion, hoarding or a cold home.

bullets: New tenancy visit within 6 weeks and starter tenancy reviews
Income maximisation and money advice referrals
Referral to adult social care, mental health services, or domestic abuse services
Reasonable adjustments to how we contact residents (large print, phone not letter, advocate present)
Priority for repairs where the household is vulnerable (e.g. loss of heating is always an emergency)
Annual welfare checks for SilverLiving residents and residents flagged as frail

blocks.p: If you believe an adult or child is at risk of harm, report it to the Safeguarding Lead the same day using the safeguarding form. If there is immediate danger, call 999.

Information about health, disability and domestic abuse is special category data under UK GDPR. It must only be seen by staff who need it. Documents containing it must carry the **Confidential** or **Highly Confidential** sensitivity label. During the Copilot pilot, staff must not put vulnerability details into prompts unless the source files are correctly labelled, and must never paste them into tools outside Microsoft 365.
No possession action for a vulnerable resident may go ahead without a sustainment review by the Head of Neighbourhoods, confirming that all reasonable support has been offered.

title: SilverLiving News - Autumn 2026 (Large Print)
summary: Large-print autumn 2026 newsletter for SilverLiving residents: Careline, staying warm, flu jabs, scam calls, coffee mornings and digital buddies.
author: P027

blocks.p: Welcome to the autumn newsletter. The evenings are drawing in, so this edition is all about staying warm, safe and in touch. As always, if you need anything, ring me or your scheme officer. We are here to help.

bullets: If your heating stops working, call us straight away. For SilverLiving residents this is **always an emergency**.
Keep your main living room at 18 to 21 degrees.
Ask us about the Winter Fuel Payment and Pension Credit. Many people miss out.

blocks.p: Please test your pendant once a month by pressing the button. The Careline team will answer and check it is working. Your annual alarm test will happen in November.
The pharmacy team will be at Linton Lodge on Tuesday 21 October and at Bearsted Court on Thursday 23 October, from 10am to 1pm. No need to book.
Silvering will never ask for your bank details over the phone to pay a refund. If you are not sure, hang up and call us on the number on your rent card.
Would you like help to video call your family or use the MySilvering app? Our volunteer digital buddies visit Linton Lodge on Friday afternoons. Ask John Stone, your scheme officer, to book a slot.
You said the Willow House lounge was too cold. We have fitted new radiators and draught-proofed the windows.

subject: Brenchley Gardens - damp and mould and residents' concerns
summary: Ward councillor raises damp, mould and repairs concerns at Brenchley Gardens; Nadia Rahman replies with the facts and invites her to the 15 October residents' meeting, then follows up with the agreed actions.

messages.body:
Dear Ms Dunmore,

I am writing as ward councillor for Shepway South. In the last month I have been contacted by six households at Brenchley Gardens about damp and mould, several with young children. One mother told me her son's asthma has got worse and that she was told to 'open the windows'. Others say repairs are started and never finished.

I would like to know how many damp and mould cases you have open on the estate, whether you are meeting the Awaab's Law timescales, and what your plan is for the blocks on the east side of the estate.

I would also welcome the chance to meet residents with you.

Yours sincerely,

Cllr Gillian Marsh

Dear Cllr Marsh,

Thank you for your email, which Rachel Dunmore has asked me to answer. I am sorry that residents have had this experience. Being told to open the windows is not acceptable and is not our policy.

Brenchley Gardens has {{fact:brenchley_homes}} homes and accounts for {{fact:damp_brenchley_share}} of all damp and mould cases we have had reported in the last 12 months. We have not met the Awaab's Law investigation timescale on every case this year, and we have told the Regulator about the breaches. We recruited a second surveyor and now run a daily breach report.

Our plan for blocks D to F is a proactive inspection of every flat by the end of November, a roof and gutter survey, and a programme of ventilation upgrades.

If you can share the six households' details (with their consent), Amira Haddad, the housing officer, will contact each of them this week.

We are holding a residents' meeting at the Brenchley Gardens Community Hall on Thursday 15 October at 6.30pm, and you would be very welcome.

Kind regards,

Nadia

Thank you, Ms Rahman. I will attend on the 15th. I have asked the six households for consent and will send details on Monday.

Gillian Marsh

Dear Cllr Marsh,

Thank you for coming on Thursday. As promised, here are the actions we agreed:

- All flats in blocks D to F to be inspected by the Damp & Mould team by 30 November.
- Block D bin store door to be repaired by 23 October.
- Gutters at 30-38 cleared by 23 October.
- Quarterly residents' meetings, the next in January 2027.
- A named contact (Amira Haddad) for every household with an open damp case.

Amira has now contacted all six households you referred. Four have open damp cases and two have been booked for inspection this week.

Kind regards,

Nadia Rahman
Head of Neighbourhoods

subject: RE: APA request - Rosie Allen, Kings Hill Quarter
summary: Ryan Tait asks Bev Saunders whether to serve a NOSP on a UC household with no APA; Bev tells him to request the APA, check the open stage 2 complaint and hardship referral, and pause escalation.

messages.body:
Hi Bev,

Quick one. Rosie Allen (RA701364, Kings Hill Quarter) is on {{sql:SELECT printf('£%.2f', balance_gbp) FROM rent_accounts WHERE account_ref = 'RA701364'}}, about 10 and a half weeks. She's on UC, no APA. She's been at hardship referral since September but nothing's come in since the 12th.

She's over the 8-week line so I was going to send the NOSP warning letter this week. OK to go ahead?

Thanks,
Ryan

Morning Ryan,

Hold off, please. A few things first:

1. She's past 8 weeks on UC with no APA. Under the policy we should have requested a managed payment when she hit 8 weeks. Please put the APA request in on the landlord portal today. That's the single thing most likely to stop the arrears growing.

2. Hannah has flagged that Ms Allen has an open stage 2 complaint (CMP-24201, communication - nobody returning her calls). Section 5 of the policy says we pause escalation while that's reviewed. Sending a NOSP warning to someone complaining we never call her back is not a good look, and the Ombudsman would agree.

3. Five in the household, children. Has money advice actually seen her? The hardship referral was in September. Chase it.

So: APA today, phone call (not a letter) this week to agree a small arrangement, and log everything. Let's review at our 1:1 on the 9th.

And when you write to her, firm but kind, please - read it back as if you were her.

Bev

Thanks Bev - APA request submitted on the portal this afternoon. DWP portal says decision within 10 working days. Rang her: no answer, left a voicemail and sent a text. I'll try again Monday.

While I was in there I noticed there are a load of UC accounts on my patch over 8 weeks with no APA. Shall I work through them?

Ryan

Yes please. It's on the 'UC no APA' tab of the dashboard. Start with the biggest balances and anyone flagged vulnerable. Same rule: check for open complaints before anything goes out.

Bev

title: Brenchley Gardens residents' meeting
summary: In-person residents' meeting at Brenchley Gardens Community Hall on damp and mould, unfinished repairs, the bin store and communication, attended by the ward councillor.
description: Open meeting for all Brenchley Gardens residents. Recorded with residents' agreement for note-taking.
agenda: Damp and mould - what we are doing
Repairs that are started and not finished
Estate issues: bin stores, gutters, lighting

transcript.text: Good evening everyone, can you hear me at the back? Great. Thank you all for coming out on a wet night. I'm Nadia Rahman, Head of Neighbourhoods. With me are Rachel Dunmore, our Director of Customer Experience, Amira who you all know, Ellie from our Damp and Mould team and Kwame from Repairs. And Councillor Marsh is here too.
Evening all. I'm here to listen and to make sure things happen afterwards.
We're recording this just so we get the notes right, nobody minds? ... OK, thank you. Let's start with damp and mould, because I know that's the big one.
Can I just say, I'm at number 9. There's mould all over the back bedroom wall and my little one sleeps in there. I haven't reported it again because of what happened last time.

Sara, I'm sorry. I'm Ellie, I'm one of the two surveyors. Please do report it - on MySilvering with a photo is quickest - and I'll pick it up. Once it's logged, the law says we have to investigate within ten working days.
Last time someone told me to open the windows.
That shouldn't have happened, and I'm sorry. We've retrained the contact centre on that. Nobody should be told it's just condensation before a surveyor has been.
The problem is the blocks on the east side. D, E and F. The top landing in E leaks every time it rains. You paint over the mould and it's back in a fortnight.

You're right, Bernard. Painting over it doesn't fix the cause. In blocks D to F we think it's a mix of the roof, the gutters and poor ventilation. So we want to inspect every flat in those blocks, not just the ones that have reported.
And we'll do that by the end of November. Ellie, is that realistic?
It's tight with two of us, but yes, if we get access.

Can I talk about repairs? I'm Frank, number 34. Gas leak in July, they capped the boiler, said a part was ordered. Five weeks with no hot water. I wrote a letter in the end. Then I get a letter saying my complaint isn't upheld!
Frank, I've read your letter. I'm not going to defend that response tonight. It's at stage 2 now and it's being looked at again properly.
Well, the boiler's fixed now, but it took my daughter ringing every day.

Kwame, Repairs. Frank, that's on us. What happened is the operative closed the job saying 'parts required' and the follow-on job never got raised. We're looking at how many times that's happened. I don't think you're the only one.
You're not, I can tell you that. Half the people on my side have had the same.
OK, estate issues. Melissa, you did the walkabout with Amira in September.
The bin store door at block D. We reported it in June. It's still broken. Foxes get in, there's rubbish everywhere. It's a small thing but it makes the whole place feel like nobody cares.
I'm really sorry, Melissa. That should have been done in July. It was missed.
I'll get it done. End of the month at the latest.
Can we have a firmer date than that? Residents have waited four months.
Fair. I'll aim for the 23rd.
And the gutters at 30 to 38. They pour over every time.
Same date, the 23rd, for the gutters.
Last thing. Keeping you informed. What would help?
Just tell us when. Not 'soon'. A date.
And a meeting like this every few months. With you lot here, not just Amira, she does her best.
Agreed. Quarterly meetings, the next one in January. And for anyone with an open damp case, Amira will be your named contact.
I'll leave my number on the table. Please take one.
Thank you everyone. We'll send out what we've agreed by Monday, and the councillor will get a copy too.

recap.summary: Residents raised damp and mould in blocks D-F, repairs left unfinished after 'parts ordered' visits, the block D bin store door broken since June, and poor communication. Silvering committed to inspecting every flat in blocks D-F by 30 November, fixing the bin store door and gutters by 23 October, quarterly residents' meetings and a named contact for open damp cases.
